notes: This is an external validation benchmark, not discovery input.
The frozen normalized-Frobenius distances predate transcription of the complete benchmark.
The L10H7-L11H10 relation was inspected before this benchmark was frozen and is retrospective evidence.

ioi.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small

copy_suppression.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding an Attention Head

families.evidence: Both heads perform copy suppression; L10H7 is characterized across the training distribution and L11H10 is the second negative head and downstream backup.
Heads attend to the indirect-object name and copy it toward the output on the IOI task.
Heads route duplicate/positional information to inhibit the repeated subject in the IOI circuit.
families.homogeneity: moderate; shared circuit role does not prove identical full-distribution function

families.evidence: L2H2 and L4H11 were the two strongest validated previous-token heads on random-token sequences; L2H9 appears in the broader IOI circuit class.
families.homogeneity: high for primary heads; extended member less strongly validated

families.evidence: L0H1 and L3H0 were strongly validated on repeated random-token sequences; L0H10 was described as a fuzzy short-range duplicate head.
families.homogeneity: high for primary heads; extended member explicitly fuzzy

families.evidence: L5H5 and L6H9 showed strong induction and copying behavior; L5H8 and L5H9 were described as fuzzy induction heads.
families.homogeneity: high for primary heads; extended members explicitly fuzzy

families.evidence: Heads compensate after primary name movers are ablated, but the source divides them into several attention/write subtypes and states that their diversity was not thoroughly investigated.
